papers.title_en: Modeling and Chasing the Energy-Efficiency Sweet Spots in Modern GPUs
papers.authors: Ayesha Afzal, Markus Manfred Li, Michael Panzlaff
papers.evidence: 研究现代GPU能效区间，提出分析模型识别能效最优点以用于资源管理
papers.tldr: 在现代异构CPU-GPU系统中，能耗已成为高性能计算的关键瓶颈，能量-求解时间效率随硬件配置和工作负载显著变化。本研究针对A40/A100/H100/H200四代GPU与Intel Ice Lake CPU系统，使用GROMACS、AMBER分子动力学及FIRESTARTER压力测试，系统探索频率调节与功率上限的影响。实验发现，能效存在非线性功率-频率缩放导致的效率“甜点”区域，并发生与架构相关的突然转变。为此，我们构建了一个可解释的分析模型，将GPU功耗分解为线性和非线性分量，从而识别出效率下降的跃迁频率。该模型紧密拟合实测数据，揭示基线功率和非线性行为是主导参数，同时表明降频比功率上限调节更有效。该工作为配置驱动的高效能HPC运行点选择提供了理论和实践指导。
papers.abstract_en: Energy consumption is a key limitation in high-performance computing on heterogeneous CPU-GPU systems. This work studies how hardware configuration affects energy-to-solution under realistic workloads. We study energy efficiency regimes using molecular dynamics benchmarks (GROMACS and AMBER) and a stress-test benchmark (FIRESTARTER) on systems with A40, A100, H100, and H200 GPUs and Intel Ice Lake CPU, varying frequency scaling and power cap. We show that energy-to-solution exhibits workload- and architecture-dependent transitions between efficient and inefficient regimes, driven by nonlinear GPU power-frequency scaling. We introduce an interpretable analytical model that decomposes GPU power into linear and nonlinear components, identifying a workload- and architecture-dependent transition frequency beyond which efficiency degrades. The model fits empirical data with low error and highlights the role of baseline power, nonlinear power behavior, and transition frequency as the dominant parameters governing energy efficiency. Power capping is generally less effective for efficiency tuning than frequency reduction, especially for workloads that operate far from thermal design power. Overall, energy-efficient HPC execution is a configuration-dependent problem with identifiable regime shifts, and we provide model-driven guidance for selecting operating points.

papers.title_en: Privacy-Preserving and Verifiable Approximate Distributed Coded Computing
papers.authors: Xavier Martínez-Luaña, Alba Gude-Santos, Manuel Fernández-Veiga, Rebeca P. Díaz-Redondo
papers.evidence: 跨联邦和去中心化设置的抗对手分布式学习模型无关框架
papers.tldr: 分布式机器学习虽然能保护数据隐私，但训练过程仍面临隐私泄露和恶意参与者攻击的双重风险。现有防御往往孤立处理隐私或完整性，且与特定模型架构强耦合。本文提出一个模型无关的统一框架，在联邦和去中心化两种范式下结合GPBACC隐私增强编码计算，分别采用鲁棒聚合和轻量级验证机制抵御恶意行为。实验证实该方法能显著减少隐私泄露并有效隔离对手，为实用安全分布式学习铺平道路。
papers.abstract_en: Distributed machine learning enables collaborative model training without centralizing data, but it also exposes learning processes to privacy leakage and malicious manipulation. Existing defenses typically address these threats in isolation and are often tailored to specific learning paradigms or model architectures, limiting their applicability in realistic deployments. In particular, federated learning and decentralized learning exhibit distinct adversarial surfaces that are rarely addressed within a unified framework. In this paper, we present a model-agnostic framework for adversary-resistant distributed learning that jointly addresses privacy preservation and malicious behavior across both federated and decentralized settings. Our approach combines paradigm-specific defense mechanisms with GPBACC, a privacy-enhancing coded computing technique applicable to arbitrary machine learning models. For federated learning, we integrate robust aggregation strategies to mitigate the impact of malicious participants, while for decentralized learning we employ approximate decode-and-compare and group testing techniques to enable lightweight verification and adversary isolation without relying on a trusted aggregator. Crucially, we evaluate the proposed framework through an explicit, attack-driven analysis. We implement representative privacy attacks and malicious behaviors, and empirically demonstrate that the combination of GPBACC with robust aggregation and verification mechanisms significantly reduces privacy leakage and improves resilience against active adversaries. These results suggest that privacy-enhancing coded computing, when combined with appropriate adversary-resistance strategies, provides a practical and deployable foundation for secure distributed machine learning.

papers.title_en: Physics-Informed Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Over Distributed Edge Devices
papers.evidence: 提出物理信息引导的联邦学习框架，将阵列流形几何作为正则项
papers.tldr: 方向估计任务受益于深度学习，但在分布式边缘设备部署面临隐私和通信挑战，联邦学习可解决但忽略阵列流形物理特性。本文提出物理信息联邦学习框架，通过流形感知正则项将导向矢量几何直接建模进本地训练，在导向空间而非标签空间惩罚差异。仿真表明该方法在iid和非iid数据下均优于多个联邦学习基线，为分布式阵列处理提供物理驱动的新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation is a fundamental array processing task that has benefited substantially from deep learning. Deploying such methods across distributed edge devices introduces privacy and communication constraints that federated learning (FL) can address. Yet, standard FL algorithms treat DoA as a generic classification problem, ignoring the underlying physics of the array manifold. To address this, we propose a physics-informed FL framework for DoA estimation that incorporates steering-vector geometry directly into the local training objective via a manifold-aware regularizer. Unlike existing FL baselines, the regularizer in our framework penalizes discrepancies in steering space rather than label space, exploiting the known geometric structure of the array manifold. We provide theoretical convergence guarantees for our framework, showing convergence to a stationary point. Simulation results confirm that our physics informed approach outperforms multiple FL baseline approaches across iid and non-iid data conditions.

papers.title_en: FLAIR: Distributed Federated Learning with Dynamic Clustering
papers.authors: Ihssan Boutebicha, Bilel Zaghdoudi, Mohamed Amine Legheraba, Maria Potop Butucaru
papers.evidence: 一种用于分布式训练的完全去中心化联邦学习协议，支持动态聚类
papers.tldr: 传统集中式与分层式联邦学习在动态无基础设施环境（如传感器网络）中面临可扩展性、弹性与单点故障等严峻挑战。FLAIR协议采用完全去中心化设计，集成基于资源感知的安全自组织聚类与簇内模型训练，并通过概率可验证的簇头选举机制优先选择高能力节点，确保公平与效率。ns-3仿真表明，在100节点静态网络中准确率达0.91，超越所有基线；90%节点失效下准确率仍高于0.85；对移动鲁棒，性能损失<2%；智能农业场景中与集中式基线仅差0.2%。FLAIR融合了去中心化扩展性与聚类结构效率，为大规模异构IoT提供鲁棒实用的联邦学习方案。
papers.abstract_en: Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving framework for distributed machine learning, yet conventional centralized and hierarchical architectures present significant challenges in terms of scalability, resilience, and single points of failure, particularly in dynamic, infrastructure-less environments such as sensor networks. To address these limitations, we introduce FLAIR, a novel, fully decentralized FL protocol that integrates dynamic, resource-aware secure and self-organized clustering with in-cluster model training. FLAIR leverages a probabilistic, verifiable cluster-head election mechanism, which is enhanced to favor nodes with greater computational and communication capabilities, thereby ensuring both fairness and efficiency. Through comprehensive simulations in ns-3, we evaluate FLAIR against centralized, hierarchical, and gossip-based FL benchmarks across four demanding scenarios. The results demonstrate the superiority of our approach: in static 100-node networks, FLAIR achieves a final accuracy of approximately 0.91, outperforming all baselines. The protocol exhibits exceptional robustness, maintaining graceful degradation with accuracy above 0.85 even under 90% node failure rates. Furthermore, it shows strong resilience to mobility, with a performance loss of less than 2% compared to static deployments. In a realistic smart farming simulation, FLAIR's accuracy is within 0.2% of the centralized baseline, confirming its practical viability. These findings validate that FLAIR successfully combines the scalability of decentralized learning with the structural efficiency of clustering, presenting a robust and high performing solution for large-scale, heterogeneous IoT systems.

papers.title_en: Air-Plan: Query-Optimized Topology Selection for Over-the-Air Decentralized Federated Learning
papers.authors: Kaushal Attaluri, Rebeca P. Diaz-Redondo, Manuel Fernandez Veiga
papers.evidence: 针对空口去中心化联邦学习的查询优化拓扑选择，提升通信效率。
papers.tldr: 空中聚合虽可加速集中式联邦学习，但在去中心化环境下缺乏对通信拓扑的系统优化。AIRPLAN框架首次将OTA-DFL拓扑选择等价为分布式查询成本优化问题，利用隐私保护的Count-Min Sketch统计估计工作负载，通过图感知成本模型选择满足准确率SLA的最低成本图。实验涵盖五类图族、三个视觉任务、四种客户端规模及多种信噪比，结果表明91.4%的工作负载中匹配预言最优拓扑，且额外开销低于1.8%。该工作为无线联邦学习与分布式查询优化的跨领域融合提供了系统化思路。
papers.abstract_en: Over-the-air (OTA) aggregation exploits the superposition property of wireless multiple-access channels to aggregate model updates from multiple devices within a single transmission slot, significantly reducing communication latency. While OTA computation has been extensively studied for centralized federated learning (FL), its integration with decentralized federated learning (DFL) remains largely unexplored, and principled communication topology selection is absent from existing work.   We present AIRPLAN, a query-optimized topology selection framework for Over-the-Air Decentralized Federated Learning (OTA-DFL). AIRPLAN establishes a formal equivalence between OTA-DFL and distributed query processing, enabling topology selection to be formulated as a cost-based query optimization problem. Using privacy-preserving Count-Min Sketch statistics, AIRPLAN estimates workload characteristics, evaluates a graph-aware cost model across candidate topologies, and selects the communication graph that minimizes training cost while satisfying a target accuracy SLA.   Experiments across five graph families, three vision benchmarks, four client scales, and multiple SNR settings show that AIRPLAN matches the oracle-optimal topology in 91.4% of workloads while introducing less than 1.8% overhead. We further derive theoretical error bounds for topology-aware sparsification, demonstrating that well-connected topologies better tolerate aggressive compression. AIRPLAN introduces a systems-oriented perspective that bridges wireless federated learning and distributed query optimization.
